text:
J.T. Miller's November headlines have been about his return to Vancouver, where he was booed and was caught chirping Elias Pettersson in a 5-1 Rangers win. On the ice, the Rangers captain is in a goal drought: none in eight games, on 3.4 expected goals.

That drought looks like bad luck. He has 4 goals on 7.6 expected this season, and the Rangers have scored 9.3 fewer goals than their chances with him on the ice. His process is strong: New York controls 63% of the 5v5 expected goals with him out there, 14.5 points better than without him. His shot still hits 93.9 mph by NHL Edge tracking, 98th percentile.

Evolving-Hockey told the same story about last season: 0.9 expected wins against -0.2 actual, with tough competition. That's two seasons now where the finishing hasn't matched the chances, which is worth noticing. But the shape of this one says the goals should come. Our range has him at 53 to 76 points, and he has 17 so far.
